title: METR Q4 2026 capability update (Nov 20): public evidence is "insufficient to rule out" drastic AI R&D acceleration within a couple of years; agents show worse judgment than experts on low-feedback tasks
author_or_publisher: METR (Kinniment, Shetty, Goodrich et al., with Beth Barnes)
quote_verbatim: We think that current public evidence is insufficient to rule out drastic AI R&D acceleration in the next couple of years.
what_is_new: Evaluations up to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra: models usually match or beat skilled human baseliners on METR coding/optimization tasks; on the combined TH1.1+TH2 suite time horizons double about every 3.6 months; model judges overrate outputs of similar or stronger models; METR says capabilities are getting harder to measure.
why_for_agiright: An independent evaluator saying it cannot rule out drastic AI R&D acceleration speaks directly to evaluation limits and recursive self-improvement oversight.
doubts: Overview and results summary read (about 12k of 200k+ characters; appendices not read). Techmeme cites MIT Technology Review (not opened). Also on metr.org: note "Measuring alignment eval tells" (Nov 16, before window, not logged). Topics index searched: METR+2026, time horizon, capability update (no match for this post).
